Here's your species' fun puzzle: you know how to save millions of lives. You can measure exactly how many. You have the money. Your governments still don't do it.

This isn't because your politicians are evil. It's because your system is built so that:

* Politicians maximize **reelection, status, and post-office careers**, not "humans continuing to exist"
* Bureaucracies maximize **budget and turf**, not "speed of cures"
* Lobbyists maximize **client profits**, not "global welfare"

You don't fix this with awareness campaigns. You've been "raising awareness" for decades and everyone is still dying. You don't fix it with white papers. Politicians use white papers to stabilize wobbly tables. You fix it by changing **what "self-interest" points at**.

This chapter describes how to legally bribe your politicians into doing the right thing:

> **Incentive Alignment Bonds (IABs)**: a way to pay for better governance without technically paying politicians, giving money to governments, or going to prison.

### The Core Problem: Good Ideas Die in Committee

![Tiny cost now, massive benefit later. Politicians are very good at the 'now' part and very bad at the 'later' part.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-core-problem-good-ideas-die-in-committee-bw-academic.jpg)

Your 1% Treaty isn't constrained by physics, biology, or money. It's constrained by **politics**, which is like being constrained by your dog's opinion on quantum mechanics except your dog can veto legislation.

No politician wants to be the one who "cut the military." Even by 1%. Even if that 1% cures cancer. The attack ads write themselves: "Senator Johnson voted to WEAKEN AMERICA."

Your system does exactly what it's incentivized to do. It's not broken. It's working perfectly. The problem is what it's optimizing for.

### What You Need: Legal Bribery

![Politician does good thing. People get healthier. Politician gets money. It's a bribe, but backwards and legal.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-what-you-need-legal-bribery-that-isn-t-technically-bribery-bw-academic.jpg)

Tell every politician on Earth:

> "Vote for a 1%-style reform. If your country actually funds it, you get: better reputation (better parties), better reelection odds (independent campaigns favor you), and better post-office career (Goldman Sachs boards, fellowships, that sort of thing)."

No backroom deals. No suitcases of cash. Just a standing, public rule: do the objectively good thing, and the world systematically rewards you.

### What IABs Are

**Incentive Alignment Bonds** are financial instruments that:

1. **Reward investors** with returns from public-good funding achieved
2. **Reward politicians** with electoral support and career benefits for voting right
3. **Fund the actual public good** from the policy outcome (self-sustaining)

![Rich people give money to politicians who save lives. The triangle of virtue signaling that actually works.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-definition-what-are-incentive-alignment-bonds-bw-academic.jpg)

Not charity (doesn't scale). Not lobbying (taken). Not "paying politicians" (illegal, also taken). IABs make investors and politicians cooperate on public goods by appealing to the only thing they respond to: self-interest.

| | Social Impact Bonds | Incentive Alignment Bonds |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Who's rewarded** | Service providers (nonprofits) | Politicians AND investors |
| **What's measured** | Service delivery outcomes | Policy adoption and funding flows |
| **Scale** | City/program level | National/global |
| **Funding source** | External (government pays) | Self-funding (policy outcome funds returns) |

### How IABs Work (Four Steps)

![How to build a legal bribery machine in four easy steps. Lawyers helped.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-how-incentive-alignment-bonds-work-the-simple-version-bw-academic.jpg)

#### Step 1: Pick a Measurable Outcome

![Things we can count right now versus things that matter later. One gets you reelected, the other gets you into heaven. Choose wisely.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-step-1-define-a-measurable-outcome-bw-academic.jpg)

**Measure funding flows, not health outcomes.** You can't attribute a cure to any specific country's funding. But you CAN measure: % of military spending redirected, total $ contributed, and politician votes on treaty passage.

Health improvements justify the policy. Funding flows are the metric for scoring, because they're what politicians control.

#### Step 2: Raise Capital

![Money goes into a trust. Trust pays out when good things happen. It's like a piggy bank that only opens when people stop dying.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-step-2-raise-capital-bw-academic.jpg)

Investors buy IABs. Capital sits in a trust. It pays out if and only if public-good targets are hit. Same structure as green bonds and catastrophe bonds.

#### Step 3: Reward Your Politicians (Indirectly)

![Save lives, get good ratings, win elections, get consulting gig at think tank. The circle of political life.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-step-3-fund-outcomes-reward-politicians-indirectly-bw-academic.jpg)

When a politician votes for a 1%-style policy and funding actually flows, the mechanism triggers:

* **Public Good Scores** rise (published by independent rating orgs)
* **Electoral support** increases (independent campaigns favor high-scorers)
* **Post-office opportunities** unlock (fellowships, boards, speaking circuits)

No money flows to politicians. What flows is **reputation, electoral advantage, and career advancement**. They're just getting credit for doing their job well. On your planet, this is apparently revolutionary.

#### Step 4: Watch Self-Interest Do the Rest

![Do good things, get points, media loves you, voters love you, you get richer and more famous. Virtue has never been so profitable.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-step-4-make-politicians-care-without-paying-them-bw-academic.jpg)

Your politicians' utility function is roughly:

> U = P(reelection) + career advancement + post-office income + legacy

IABs make supporting 1%-equivalent policies **strictly increase all four terms**. No altruism required. The privately optimal action (maximize personal payoff) and the socially optimal action (reduce suffering) become identical. You've essentially tricked your leaders into saving lives by making it profitable.

### The Three-Layer Architecture (How to Not Go to Prison)

![Three different ways to pay politicians to be nice, stacked on top of each other like a very boring wedding cake.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-4a-the-three-layer-architecture-how-to-not-go-to-prison-bw-academic.jpg)

You cannot legally say "support Bill #XYZ123 and get paid." That's bribery. But you *can* create a system where politicians who support a **class of pro-social policies** systematically get more of everything they want. The trick: rule-based, universal, announced in advance.

#### Layer A: Scoring (Data Only)

![Your state's health plus your voting record equals your Good Boy Points. Gold stars for senators who behave.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-layer-a-outcome-and-policy-scoring-data-only-bw-academic.jpg)

An independent org assigns each politician a **Public Good Score** based on: votes for 1%-equivalent measures, bill sponsorship, blocking harmful reversals, and actual funding flows.

Critical: **don't tie scores to "The 1% Treaty" specifically.** Define a policy class: "Policies that reallocate ≥1% of military spending into independently governed pragmatic clinical trials." Any politician supporting *any* matching policy gets credit.

The scoring is public, rules-based, and non-partisan. Like a credit score for your soul, except useful.

#### Layer B: Electoral Benefits (Separate Actors)

![Your score gets broadcast to every organization with money and opinions. Peer pressure, but with Super PACs.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-layer-b-electoral-and-reputational-benefits-separate-actors-bw-academic.jpg)

Independent PACs and 501(c)(4)s commit **in advance** to favor high-scoring politicians. NGOs publish annual rankings. Conferences invite high-scorers. Awards go to high-scorers. Your politicians love awards even more than they love conferences, which is saying something.

The goal: make the Public Good Score as influential as Moody's credit ratings. Moody's can downgrade a country and suddenly borrowing costs spike. If your Public Good Score achieves similar salience, high score = respect, invitations, book deals. Low score = awkward questions at dinner parties.

This is exactly how NRA grades and Chamber of Commerce ratings already work. Same mechanism, different metric: "did you vote for policies that measurably reduced human suffering?"

#### Layer C: Post-Office Careers (The Goldman Sachs Board Problem)

![Old way: help corporations, get cushy job. New way: help humans, get cushy job. Same job, different resume line.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-layer-c-post-office-career-ben-bw-academic.jpg)

After your politicians leave office, they want prestigious jobs. This is called "the revolving door" and it's usually pointed at whoever paid the most lobbyists. You can point it somewhere else.

Foundations and think tanks establish: "Eligibility for fellowships and advisory roles requires a Public Good Score above threshold X." Politicians know this rule in advance. Support reform = WHO boards and Aspen fellowships. Oppose it = you'll have to explain why you voted against curing diseases. The revolving door, but spinning toward "saved lives."

#### Legal Entity Separation

| Layer | Entity Type | Can Do | Cannot Do |
|:------|:------------|:-------|:----------|
| Scoring | 501(c)(3) research org | Metrics, dashboards, public data | Support/oppose candidates |
| Electoral | 501(c)(4), PAC, Super PAC | Independent expenditures for high-scorers | Coordinate with candidates |
| Post-office | Foundations, think tanks | Set eligibility criteria | Condition grants on specific votes |

![Three separate organizations that definitely don't coordinate but somehow all reward the same behavior. Legal loopholes are beautiful things.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-legal-entity-separation-bw-academic.jpg)

Three separate entities that definitely don't coordinate but somehow all reward the same behavior. Your species invented this structure. It's one of your better ideas.

### Worked Example: How Senator Smith Votes Yes

Abstract mechanisms are great for economists and terrible for everyone else. Here's how IABs actually work on a real human politician.

#### The Scoring System

![Vote to cure cancer: plus 10 points. Vote to bomb Yemen: minus 15 points. It's like Weight Watchers, but for your soul.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-public-good-score-bw-academic.jpg)

Each politician gets a Public Good Score based on their voting record:

| Bill Type | Yes Vote | No Vote |
|:----------|:---------|:--------|
| Increase % reallocation to 1% Treaty Fund | +15 | -15 |
| Protect existing funding | +10 | -10 |
| Expand treaty to more countries | +10 | -10 |
| Cut funding or % | -20 | +5 |

![Get 60 points, unlock Tier 3 campaign spending. Get 80 points, unlock consulting jobs. Politics as a video game.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-how-score-translates-to-utility-bw-academic.jpg)

Your score determines what you get:

| Score | PAC Spending | Post-Office Tier | Annual Income |
|:------|:-------------|:-----------------|:--------------|
| ≥75 | +$2M for you | Tier 1: WHO boards, Aspen fellowships | $500K+ |
| 60-74 | +$500K for you | Tier 2: Brookings, RAND, university chairs | $200-400K |
| 50-59 | $0 | Tier 3: Standard revolving door | $150-300K |
| 40-49 | $500K to opponent | Tier 3 | $150-300K |
| <40 | $2M to opponent | Tier 3 | $150-300K |

It's like a video game skill tree, except the XP comes from not killing people.

#### The Setup

[VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds.qmd) have raised {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} from investors who want {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns. That money has funded:

- A referendum showing 70% of Americans support reallocating 1% of military spending to pragmatic clinical trials
- A lobbying campaign that's converted several military contractors (they did the math on their own mortality)
- The Public Good Scoring system described above, tracking every federal legislator

Senator Smith (R-Texas) is up for reelection in 2026. The 1% Treaty Implementation Act is coming to a vote. 

![Senator Smith's report card: below average score, barely passing reelection odds, medium-quality retirement prospects. Her mother is disappointed.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-setup-bw-academic.jpg)

**Her current stats:**

- Public Good Score: 45 (below Senate median of 52)
- Current P(reelection): 55%
- Expected post-office tier: 3
- Expected post-office income: $200K/year

#### The Old Calculus (Without IABs)

| Vote Yes | Vote No |
|:---------|:--------|
| Attack ads: "Smith voted to WEAKEN AMERICA" | Safe from military lobby attacks |
| Defense contractors fund opponent | Defense contractors fund you |
| No immediate upside | Status quo maintained |
| Benefits arrive in 10 years | Costs arrive never |

**Expected utility of No vote:** $U = 0.55 \cdot \text{Office} + \$200K/\text{year} \cdot 20\text{yrs} + \text{Medium Legacy}$

Result: Vote no. Obviously.

#### The New Calculus (With IABs)

**If Smith votes YES:**

- VoteRecord: +15 points (major treaty vote)
- New Score: 45 + 15 = 60 → jumps to 72 with multiplier for being early supporter
- P(reelection): 55% → 62% (score boost + $500K independent support)
- Post-office tier: 3 → 2 (with path to Tier 1 if she becomes a champion)
- Expected post-office income: $200K → $300K/year

**If Smith votes NO:**

- VoteRecord: -15 points
- New Score: 45 - 15 = 30
- P(reelection): 55% → 48% (score penalty + $2M goes to opponent)
- Post-office tier: Stuck at 3
- Attack ads funded: "Smith voted AGAINST the cure your family needs"

![Vote yes: 73% chance you keep your job, make millions after. Vote no: 55% chance you're unemployed next year. Choose carefully, Senator.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-new-calculus-with-iabs-bw-academic.jpg)

**The math:**

$$
\Delta U_{\text{Yes vs No}} = 0.14 \cdot \text{Office} + \$100K/\text{year} \cdot 20\text{yrs} + \text{Legacy Boost}
$$

That's a +14 percentage point swing in reelection odds and +$2M in lifetime post-office earnings. 

Result: Vote yes. The math changed.

#### What Actually Happens

![All the math a senator does before deciding how to vote. Turns out they can count when money's involved.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-what-actually-happens-bw-academic.jpg)

1. **Pre-vote**: Smith's staff models the yes vote. Score jumps to 72. Reelection odds rise 7 points.
2. **Lobbying meeting**: Military lobby threatens. But three major contractors already support the treaty (270% returns beat 8%). Threat is empty.
3. **Campaign finance**: Health advocacy Super PACs have committed $50M nationally. At score 72, she gets $2M. A no vote sends that $2M to her opponent.
4. **Constituent mail**: 70% of Texans voted yes in the referendum. Voting against that means explaining why you think they're wrong about not wanting to die.
5. **The vote**: Smith votes yes. So do 67 others. Treaty passes.

#### Post-Treaty

![Senator Smith's career trajectory before and after voting yes. One line goes up, one line stays flat. Guess which one she prefers.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-post-treaty-the-numbers-bw-academic.jpg)

| Metric | Before | After |
|:-------|:-------|:------|
| Public Good Score | 45 | 78 |
| P(reelection) | 55% | 68% |
| Independent support | $0 | $3M |
| Post-office tier | 3 | 1 |
| Post-office income | $200K/yr | $500K/yr |

Smith wins reelection by 12 points. Joins the WHO Advisory Board. Chairs the Aspen Health Initiative. All because she did math instead of listening to lobbyists.

The flywheel spins. Each expansion increases the stakes, increases the score differential, makes voting yes even more dominant:

| Year | Treaty % | Revenue | Bondholder Payout |
|:-----|:---------|:--------|:------------------|
| 1 | 1% | {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} | {{< var victory_bond_annual_payout >}} |
| 3 | 2% | $54B | $5.4B |
| 5 | 5% | $135B | $13.5B |

![Where $27 billion goes: some to investors, some to politicians, most to actually curing diseases. Everyone gets a slice of the virtue pie.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-math-for-victory-incentive-alignment-bond-investors-bw-academic.jpg)

### Why This Isn't Bribery

![Bribery: pay someone to betray the public. This thing: pay someone to help the public. Spot the difference, legally speaking.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-why-this-is-not-bribery-legally-speaking-bw-academic.jpg)

Four reasons your lawyers will care about:

1. **No one is paid to break a duty.** IABs reward compliance: "do your job better and we'll tell everyone you did." That's a performance review, not a bribe.
2. **Rules are universal and ex-ante.** Same rules for all politicians, all parties, announced publicly in advance. No envelopes in parking garages.
3. **No money goes to politicians.** They benefit indirectly: better scores, electoral support, nicer career options. This is how democracy is supposed to work.
4. **Scores are based on public voting records.** Did they vote YES? That's verifiable and ungameable. The {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} fund flows automatically based on treasury inflows. Pure math.

Bribery **corrupts** alignment. IABs **create** it.

### How IABs Connect to Your 1% Treaty

![The machine that turns 'we should cure diseases' into 'Senator Smith gets $4 million if she votes yes.' Translation is everything.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-how-this-plugs-into-the-1-trea-bw-academic.jpg)

Treaties are just PDFs with fancy letterheads unless you give countries a reason to follow them. IABs provide the missing mechanism:

1. **Scoring.** Track which politicians voted for 1%-equivalent policies. Credit or blame in a format voters understand.
2. **Rewarding early adopters.** Move first = higher score = career benefits. "Being first to do the right thing" becomes "being first to get the career benefits."
3. **Creating pressure.** Low-performing countries get awkward questions at international summits. Your politicians hate awkward questions at international summits.

Your 1% Treaty describes the **what**. IABs supply the **how**.

### Objections

#### "Won't politicians game the metrics?"

![Things people can lie about versus things they can't. Turns out politicians are better at lying than numbers are.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-objection-1-won-t-politicians-game-the-metrics-bw-academic.jpg)

Yes. Your politicians game everything. The question is whether gaming it is harder than just doing the right thing. Scoring uses **public voting records** and **verified funding flows**. To game these, you'd need to falsify your own vote (public record) or pretend funding flowed when it didn't (treasury records are public). These are orders of magnitude harder to fake than self-reported ESG compliance.

#### "Isn't this just rich people buying policy?"

![Three separate boxes to keep politicians from stealing money directly. They have to steal it indirectly now, which takes longer.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-objection-2-isn-t-this-just-rich-people-buying-policy-bw-academic.jpg)

Wealthy actors *already* buy policy. Pharma spends $300M/year lobbying. Defense contractors spend more. The question isn't "should money influence policy?" but "can you point that influence toward measurable welfare instead of narrow interests?"

The safeguards: no quid pro quo (standing rules only), universal and ex-ante (same for all parties), no cash to politicians (indirect benefits only), and the metric is suffering reduced, not interests served. The direction of distortion is reversed.

Honest admission: yes, IAB funders will have more influence over which public goods get prioritized. That's true of all philanthropy. The Gates Foundation has more influence over malaria policy than a random person. The question is whether that influence is transparent, measurable, and auditable. IABs satisfy all three.

#### "What if politicians reverse the policy?"

![What happens to your score when you do good things for a while and then suddenly decide to do bad things instead. The graph goes down quite dramatically.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-objection-3-what-if-politicians-pocket-the-career-rewards-th-bw-academic.jpg)

Score decay. Vote to reverse funding and your Public Good Score tanks. The same mechanism that rewarded you for supporting the policy punishes you for killing it. "You voted yes once" is worth less than "you defended the funding for five years." You can't prevent all backsliding, but you can make it expensive.

#### "Is this realistic globally?"

![How countries copy each other's homework after seeing someone else get a good grade. Like peer pressure, but for governments.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-objection-4-is-this-realistic-at-a-global-scale-bw-academic.jpg)

It doesn't have to start global. One or two pilot countries (Portugal, Costa Rica, New Zealand) adopt a limited 1%-style policy. Funding flows are verified. Leaders get invited to better conferences. Other countries notice and copy what works. FOMO is a powerful force in international relations.

Credit ratings started as one guy in the 1800s publishing opinions about railroad bonds. Now Moody's can tank a country's economy with a press release. Same scaling path: proof of concept, early movers, FOMO among laggards, new normal.

### Why This Matters

![Paying politicians to do their jobs properly. Like a chore chart for adults who run countries.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-why-this-matters-for-ending-war-and-disease-bw-academic.jpg)

Ending war and disease is not a scientific problem. It's a governance problem. You already know how to prevent pandemics, run cheap trials, and redirect 1% of war budgets. What's missing is a credible way to **reward** your governments for doing these things using the only language they speak: self-interest.

IABs change the game from "hope someone in power cares" to "make caring the best selfish move a leader can make."

### Why 10% Goes to Political Incentives {#sec-why-ten-pct-scaling-engine}

![The plan to gradually stop buying bombs versus the four reasons we'll probably keep buying bombs anyway.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-goal-isn-t-a-1-treaty-the-goal-is-100-bw-academic.jpg)

Your 1% treaty is the proof of concept. The endgame is redirecting *most* of military spending to health. That doesn't happen automatically. Without sustained political pressure, your treaty stalls at 1% forever, like your Paris Agreement.

The {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} allocation creates a **political ratchet** that only moves one direction:

![How much money politicians get for being nice increases as they're nicer. By the end, they get 270 billion dollars for not killing people.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-iabs-are-the-political-ratchet-bw-academic.jpg)

| Treaty Level | IAB Political Funding (10%) | Research Funding (80%) | Effect |
|:-------------|:----------------------------|:-----------------------|:-------|
| 1% | {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_annual >}}/year | {{< var dih_treasury_to_medical_research_annual >}}/year | Politicians rewarded for passage |
| 5% | $13.6B/year | $109B/year | Defense industry pivots to health |
| 10% | $27.2B/year | $218B/year | War becomes economically obsolete |
| 50% | $136B/year | $1.09T/year | Global transformation |
| 100% | $272B/year | $2.18T/year | Full redirection achieved |

At 100%, IABs would fund **$270B/year** in political incentives. More than all current global lobbying combined. "Support pragmatic clinical trials" would become the single most rewarded political position on your planet.

![Spend 270 billion bribing politicians to unlock 2.16 trillion for medicine. Like using a small key to open a very large door full of money.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-math-changes-everything-bw-academic.jpg)

**Without IABs:**

![What happens over fifty years if we do nothing special versus if we pay politicians to care. One line stays flat, the other goes up like a rocket.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-the-alternative-is-stagnation-bw-academic.jpg)

- Year 1-3: Treaty passes. Celebration.
- Year 4-7: Defense lobby regroups. No expansion.
- Year 16+: Treaty becomes another Paris Agreement. Nice symbol. Everyone ignores it.

**With IABs:**

- Year 1-3: Treaty passes. Politicians rewarded.
- Year 4-7: Politicians compete to expand to 2%.
- Year 8-15: 5% treaty. Defense contractors pivot.
- Year 50+: Full redirection. Disease: solved.

The {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} isn't a cost. It's the engine. Without it, you get a one-time win. With it, you get compounding political pressure that makes each expansion easier than the last.

### Beyond the 1% Treaty

![The four boxes you need to tick before you can bribe governments into solving global problems. Apparently you can't just bribe them willy-nilly.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-beyond-the-1-treaty-iabs-as-a-general-governance-tool-bw-academic.jpg)

The same architecture works for any global coordination problem where the public good is measurable, politicians control the outcome, benefits are diffuse, and costs are concentrated. That describes most of the problems that could end your civilization:

| Domain | Metric (already exists) | IAB Makes Career-Optimal |
|:-------|:------------------------|:-------------------------|
| **Climate** | UNFCCC emissions data | "Vote for emissions cuts" |
| **Nuclear** | START treaty warhead counts | "I reduced our arsenal" |
| **Pandemic** | WHO Joint External Evaluation | "I funded preparedness" |

Same pattern: existing metric, scoring system, electoral support for high-scorers, prestige positions for leaders who governed well. See the [academic paper](../appendix/incentive-alignment-bonds-paper.qmd) for formal treatment.

### Summary

![How to make politicians care about the future by promising them good jobs after they stop being politicians. Turns out they like money that comes later too.](/assets/images/incentive-alignment-bonds/incentive-alignment-bonds-section-summary-what-iabs-actually-are-bw-academic.jpg)

IABs don't change human nature. They redirect it.

1. **They solve political economy.** Concentrated losers lobby harder than diffuse beneficiaries. IABs concentrate benefits on politicians who support good policies.
2. **They're legal.** Three-layer architecture avoids bribery law. No money to officials.
3. **They scale.** One country, then FOMO.
4. **They're self-reinforcing.** 1% → 2% → 5% → each expansion increases IAB funding, which drives the next expansion.
5. **They generalize.** Climate, nuclear risk, pandemics. Same architecture, different metric.

You're not asking your politicians to be saints. You're just making "save millions of lives" and "advance my career" point in the same direction. The rest is self-interest doing what self-interest does.
